title: Foreign Disclosure Officer (II/III) (Col to Capt) and (CWO5 to WO) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
15. MOS 0580, Foreign Disclosure Officer (II/III) (Col to Capt) and (CWO5 to
WO) FMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Foreign Disclosure Officers (FDOs) are officially
designated in writing by a command, unit, or agency with delegated disclosure
authority to regulate disclosures of classified military information (CMI),
controlled unclassified information (CUI), technology, and equipment to
foreign nationals/organizations in accordance with applicable policies. FDOs
require training in foreign disclosure policy, considerations, and strategies
to protect national security interests and strengthen relations with foreign
allies. DC PP&O will assign this MOS as an FMOS.

    b. Prerequisites. Security requirement: minimum of secret clearance.
The primary command FDO requires a T5 or T5R investigation.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Marine Corps Foreign Disclosure Officer Course (SSC
OB2), managed by PP&O.

        (2) Receive an appointment letter as an FDO from the commander or
head of an organization with delegated disclosure authority.

            (3) Recommended additional training:

            (a) Defense Intelligence Enterprise Foreign Disclosure Officer
Course (DIA-INT-2300).

                (b) Security Cooperation Workforce Basic Level Certification.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Establishes and maintains the commands foreign disclosure program
in accordance with MCO 5510.20C.

        (2) Applies foreign disclosure policy, best practices, and training
in determining information, training, technology, equipment, and capabilities
to be shared with foreign governments, entities, and non-governmental and
international organizations.




                                           1-41                         Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Plans and reviews foreign national access to information,
equipment, and capabilities during visits.

        (4) Prepares delegation of disclosure authority letters guiding U.S.
personnel interaction with foreign nationals during training, exercises,
operations, and programs.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
